text:
GENERATE BURST EN4-SLPG -- Run C-9 Phase 2 (Matt R-C9-137): the PAINTED TEXTURE of a 3D CREATURE, sheet 1. task_id "EN4-SLPG".

IMAGE 1 is a sheet of 8 renders of ONE 3D model of a serpent-bodied creature with an upright human-like upper body and two arms, its long snake body lying along the ground behind it standing still, seen from above, looking down at 53 degrees, on flat pure #00ff00. Top row, left to right: turned away toward the upper right (north-east); turned away toward the upper left (north-west); seen from BEHIND, tail toward the viewer (north); in profile, head toward the viewer's LEFT (west). Bottom row, left to right: in profile, head toward the viewer's RIGHT (east); turned toward the lower left (south-west); turned toward the lower right (south-east); head-on, FACING THE VIEWER (south). They are renders of the model: every OUTLINE, POSE, POSITION and SIZE is correct and must not change; the surface is flat, smooth and blurry.
IMAGE 2 is the creature's approved model sheet: a lean serpent-bodied caster: a long narrow flat-topped SNAKE'S HEAD with small slit-pupilled pale yellow-green eyes and a low frill of thin spines folded flat down the back of the skull and neck; a lean human-like torso and two long thin arms with four long clawed fingers; small fine scales, dull deep teal-green and slate along the back, the arms, the head and the top of the serpent body, broken by darker mottled olive-black bands across the serpent body; a broad PALE cream-ivory belly-plate of overlapping scutes from the throat down the front of the torso and along the whole underside of the snake body to the pointed tail; a few patches of ragged pale dead skin peeling at the shoulders; a short ragged wrap of faded LAPIS-BLUE cloth around the hips where the snake body begins; a few strings of small bone beads across the chest. IMAGE 3 is a STYLE reference ONLY: copy its HAND (the dark ink line that varies in weight, transparent watercolour washes that pool and granulate, fine hatching, cream paper highlights); copy nothing else from it -- it shows a person.
Use image_gen in EDIT mode on IMAGE 1 and deliver ONE 1536x1024 sheet in which EVERY view is repainted as the creature of IMAGE 2 seen from that direction, in IMAGE 3's hand, inside exactly that view's outline, position and size.
THIS PAINTING BECOMES THE MODEL'S TEXTURE: it is projected back onto the 3D model from these cameras and blended into one texture. So: ONE creature in 8 views, not 8 creatures -- the same surface, the same plates, joints and claws in every view; any disagreement between views becomes a seam.
Paint the SURFACE, not the lighting: soft even light; no cast shadows, no dark side, no rim light, no shading that belongs to one viewpoint. Tone comes from its own colours, the pen hatching and the washes. Stay inside every outline; change no outline, leg, claw, tail or tooth position. Add NOTHING IMAGE 2 does not show.
THE MARKER: a corroded BRASS ARMLET engraved with hour-marks around its LEFT upper arm ONLY, just below the shoulder, exactly where IMAGE 1 shows it; never on the right arm.
BACKGROUND: keep the background flat pure #00ff00, as in IMAGE 1. If the image model returns a darker or gradient background anyway, DO NOT spend a retry on it and still deliver the image: the views are cut out afterwards by their exact 3D outlines. Spend retries ONLY on the faults named below.

Two image_gen EDIT calls: variants a and b. ONE retry per variant only if a view's outline, pose, facing or position changed, a view is missing, the creature differs between views, or the marker is on the wrong side or missing -- name the reason. Never retry for the background colour. Copy outputs to out/EN4-SLPG_a.png and out/EN4-SLPG_b.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "EN4-SLPG"; images = the files with prompt, references (role + path) and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.

references.role: IMAGE 1 -- the sheet to EDIT (8 views at 52.95 deg of the 3D creature at rest; outlines correct, surface flat)
IMAGE 2 -- the creature's approved model sheet: the look
IMAGE 3 -- STYLE reference ONLY (Matt-supplied): the HAND to copy; never its character, costume, staff, bag or pose
